newsitem.title: CHINA: China to write off $3.6 bln in bad debts in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China to write off $3.6 bln in bad debts in 1997.

text.p: China's state commercial banks would write off 30 billion yuan ($3.6 billion) in bad debts of state enterprises in 1997, an official at the State Economic and Trade Commission said on Thursday.
State commercial banks would write off 20 billion yuan in bad debts of state firms this year, the official told Reuters. He declined to give further details.
China has been struggling with its money-losing state enterprises, trying to modernise them or sell them off.
About one percent of China's estimated 100,000 state enterprises are hopelessly in debt and unlikely to find buyers, according to some estimates.
The government has been reluctant to push many of these firms into bankruptcy due to fears of mass unemployment and social unrest.

It has so far used its bankruptcy law for smaller, less sensitive companies. But the number of bankruptcies in China -- unheard of for almost four decades -- was expected to more than double to 5,200 this year, bankruptcy expert Cao Siyuan has predicted.
